Country.evidence_source: Further quantitative research examining larger proportions and cross sections of L/B/G youth in Aotearoa/New Zealand, and overseas, is needed to identify which of these resiliency factors may be most influential in stemming L/B/G suicide stressors.

Area.evidence_source: Given that such positive resolutions are born from resiliency factors, the authors call for more emphasis on resiliency. All L/B/G youth grow up in heterosexist societies, thus one could argue that all L/B/G youth are "at risk." Resiliency enables the identification of how L/B/G youth can be helped to survive a heterosexist world. The findings of this study, while in need of verification due to the small sample size, suggest that more accurate positive portrayal of L/B/G people and issues in mass media may be invaluable to resiliency. Positive representations have the potential to provide role models, and accurate information about homosexuality (fortifying resiliency factors), whilst simultaneously reducing social isolation, and heterosexism (minimising risk factors). By troubling heterosexist stereotypes about L/B/G people, such media exposure also may have the capacity to reduce suicide risk by providing caregivers of L/B/G youth more accurate information about their sexuality and thus possibly reducing the chance that they will reject/isolate their children. Organisations like Parents and Friends of Lesbians and Gays (PFLAG) may likewise be effective in reducing suicide risk. Such organisations provide forums for caregivers to debunk false stereotypes about L/B/G people (reducing heterosexism), and can help them come to terms with their child's sexuality and, therefore, minimise the risk of rejection and ensuing social withdrawal. PFLAG and other similar groups, not only minimise the chance of heterosexism, rejection and social isolation (and the ensuing internal- ised homophobia, depression, and substance abuse), but they may further bolster resiliency by providing family role models, increasing social support, and self-esteem for L/B/G youth. L/B/G support groups may also achieve these goals. By providing more accurate information about L/B/G sexualities, and HIV, these groups may also help minimise heterosexism, and the associated internalised homophobia, depression, HIV anxiety, and substance abuse (especially by providing youth with alternative venues for socialising other than bars and clubs). Support groups may further decrease suicide risk by providing positive young role models, fortifying social support, and providing advice, welfare and legal support for L/B/G youth.
